name: Facet
text: Build the Excava interface in Figma as a clickable prototype first. It lets us test navigation, hierarchy, and interaction flows before writing a single line of code, catching usability flaws early when they’re cheap to fix. The trade-off is slower initial setup than sketching on paper, but we gain a living artifact we can share, iterate on, and hand off to engineers with clear specs.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The Figma prototype risks users mistaking the polished demo for the real interface—missing states, edge cases, and latency hide behind glossy screens. A better alternative is a live HTML/CSS prototype with real data feeds, exposing actual performance and gaps early. Settle this by testing both: measure how often users confuse the Figma mock for the real thing versus how quickly the HTML prototype reveals flaws.
